transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah, hi. I guess... I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage recently, and... well, the yard is actually a lot bigger than we thought. There's this huge oak tree in the back, and our neighbor keeps complaining about the leaves blowing onto his driveway. He drives this pristine vintage Corvette, which, honestly, why park it outside if you're so worried about leaves, right? He's out there with a leaf blower every single morning at 7 AM. 

But anyway, yeah, I just feel like every small mistake I make at work proves I’m completely useless and just... deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me. I'm waiting tables right now, and the other day I accidentally dropped a tray of water glasses. The ice went everywhere, under the booths... and they have that really cheap carpeting in the dining room that takes forever to dry. It smells like old soup when it gets wet. I don't know why the owner doesn't just put in hardwood or tile, it would be so much easier to sweep up at closing time. We're always there an extra hour just vacuuming. So, yeah... I don't know.
How long have you been feeling like you're useless and deserving of bad things?

Well, the really depressed, guilty feelings... I'd say it's been about a year and two months of feeling like this. Which, actually, is exactly when they hired the new manager at the restaurant. Gary. He's the one who decided we all needed to wear these awful polyester uniforms instead of just our own black shirts. Polyester doesn't breathe at all, you know? Especially when you're carrying hot plates back and forth from the kitchen all night. 

The kitchen is always like eighty-five degrees anyway because the ventilation hood above the fryers has been making this horrible rattling noise and barely working since Thanksgiving. The repair guy came out once, looked at it with a flashlight for maybe five minutes, and said he needed to order a special part from Germany or something. That was months ago. I bet he never even ordered it, he just wanted the call-out fee. But yeah... it's been about a year and two months of just feeling completely worthless like that.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um, pleasure? No, not really. I mean, most days there's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Just carrying plates, smiling at customers because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. Which is hard, because you have to smile for tips. 

And tips have been terrible lately, honestly. Ever since they started doing that construction on 4th Street, people just don't want to deal with the parking. They blocked off the whole right lane, and those orange barrels have been sitting there for three weeks. I saw a guy in a delivery truck clip one of them the other day and it rolled all the way down the hill into the intersection. The city planning in this town is just a joke. They repaved Elm Street last year and it already has potholes big enough to swallow a tire. My buddy Dave hit one in his Civic and bent the rim. He had to pay like three hundred dollars to get it fixed, and the city wouldn't even reimburse him. But yeah, I just... I don't really enjoy much of anything anymore. It's just empty.
Are there any activities that you still look forward to or feel excited about?

Um... excited about? Look forward to? Not really. I mean, I used to... I used to joke around with the regulars a lot. We had this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who came in every Tuesday and ordered the exact same thing—meatloaf with extra gravy, but the gravy had to be in a separate little boat, not touching the meat. He was so particular about it. One time the new cook, Ricky, just poured it all over the top, and Mr. Henderson actually sent it back. Ricky got so mad, he threw his spatula at the wall and it left this grease stain that's still there. The owner tried to scrub it off with bleach, but it just sort of smeared it around and made the paint look lighter in that one spot. It's a weird shade of yellow anyway, kind of like old mustard.

But yeah, I don't... I don't really do that anymore. Joke around, I mean. Now I mostly just keep my face straight, take their orders, and say only what I have to. Even after work, I used to text my brother, you know, just to vent about the shift or whatever. He lives out in Denver now. They get so much snow out there. He sent me a picture last winter where the snow was literally up to his porch light. I don't know how people deal with that. I hate shoveling. It wrecks your lower back, and those ergonomic shovels they sell at the hardware store are a complete rip-off. They're like forty bucks and the plastic cracks the second you hit a piece of ice. 

Anyway, I just let his messages sit now. I see them pop up on my phone, but I just... I don't feel the pull to answer them. So, no, I don't really look forward to anything.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Nervous? Or on edge? Um... no, I wouldn't say I feel nervous. I just feel... heavy. And tired. Though, speaking of being on edge, you should see the new hostess we hired last week, Sarah. She is constantly pacing back and forth by the front door like she's waiting for the health inspector to walk in. Which, honestly, wouldn't be the worst thing because the walk-in cooler has been holding at like forty-two degrees instead of under forty. I told Gary about it, but he just said to keep the door shut. 

But Sarah, she jumps every time the phone rings. It's one of those old-school phones with the really loud, shrill bell. The plastic receiver is all cracked because Ricky dropped it on the tile floor back in March. Tile floors in restaurants are the worst, by the way. They get so slippery when they're wet, and the non-slip mats we have are curling up at the edges. I tripped over one carrying a tray of water glasses and soaked my pants right at the start of a double shift. Walking around in wet polyester for ten hours is... well, it's miserable. It chafes so bad. 

But yeah, I don't really feel nervous myself. Just... flat, I guess. I don't have the energy to be on edge.
Do you ever feel any kind of happiness or joy?

Happiness? Joy? Um... no. Like I was saying before, most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's just like I'm going through the motions, you know? Carrying the plates, smiling at people because I'm supposed to, but there's no actual good feeling behind it. 

Which reminds me, I actually broke a plate yesterday. It was one of the big oval ones we use for the fisherman's platter. They're so heavy, and the dishwasher, Hector, he always stacks them too high on the rack. I've told him a hundred times, if you stack them past the metal guard, they're going to slide. But he just puts his headphones in and ignores everyone. He listens to this really intense techno music. I can hear the bass bleeding through his earbuds all the way from the prep station. I don't know how he doesn't have permanent hearing damage. My uncle listened to loud music his whole life, and now he has to wear these tiny little hearing aids that cost him like four grand. He lost one in his yard once while he was raking leaves, and we spent three hours crawling around in the grass looking for it. We never found it. He thinks a squirrel took it. 

But yeah, joy? No. I don't feel anything good. I'm just smiling because it's my job.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?

Harming myself? Wished I was dead? Um... I mean, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes... like when I'm lying awake in bed before an early shift. Those early shifts are brutal. I have to set my alarm for 4:15 AM. I use my phone alarm, but the default sounds are so obnoxious. I tried changing it to the harp sound, thinking it would be more peaceful, but now I just associate harps with pure dread. 

Have you ever actually seen a harp up close? They have so many strings, like forty-something strings, and I don't understand how anyone remembers which one is which. I went to an orchestra concert once when I was in college, for a music appreciation credit, and the harpist just sat there for like twenty minutes not playing anything, just waiting for her one part. It seemed incredibly boring. The seats in that auditorium were terrible, too—that scratchy red velvet that makes your back sweat and leaves little fuzzies all over your shirt. I had to use a lint roller in the car afterward. Lint rollers are another thing that have gotten so cheap lately. You peel off one layer and half the time it rips unevenly and you waste three sheets just trying to get a clean edge. 

Anyway, what was I... oh, right. Lying awake before the early shift. Yeah, I just stare at the ceiling and sometimes I think it would just be so much easier if I didn't wake up. If the alarm just didn't go off and I could just fade out, so I wouldn't have to keep failing at everything, you know? But no, no actual plan to hurt myself.
Do you often think about death or dying?

Death? Dying? I mean, I think I just said... like, I don't sit around planning how to do it. I don't have a plan to hurt myself. But yeah, it's just that feeling when I'm lying there in the dark, staring at the ceiling before my alarm goes off. The ceiling in my bedroom has those little popcorn bumps on it. They painted over it before I moved in, but they did a terrible job, so there are these weird flat spots where the roller pressed too hard. 

My landlord, Mr. Henderson, he refuses to hire actual professionals for anything. He tried to fix the leaky faucet in my kitchen himself last month and ended up breaking the valve, so the water had to be shut off for two whole days. I had to shower at the gym. And I hate the gym showers. The water pressure is like a pressure washer, and the soap dispensers are always empty or filled with this pink stuff that smells like industrial floor cleaner. It reminds me of the cleaner we use at the restaurant for the grease traps. That smell just sticks to your skin for hours, no matter how hard you scrub.

But yeah, when I'm just lying there, looking at that ceiling... I just think about how much easier it would be if I just didn't wake up. If I could just... stop. Stop having to go to work, stop having to keep trying and failing at everything. It just feels like it would be a relief, you know? But I don't have a plan to make it happen.
Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of pleasure?

Pleasure? Small things? Um... I don't think so. Like, I used to actually get a little bit of a kick out of joking around with the regulars at the restaurant. There's this one guy, Mr. Abernathy, who comes in every Tuesday and orders the meatloaf. He always asks for extra gravy on the side, but then he never even touches it. It just sits there congealing in the little metal ramekin. Those ramekins are a total nightmare to wash, by the way. If the gravy dries out, it turns into actual cement. You have to soak them in boiling water for like an hour, and the hot water at the restaurant takes forever to kick in. You turn the knob and just stand there freezing your hands off while you wait. 

But yeah, I used to joke with him about it. And I used to text my brother as soon as my shift was over, just to vent or whatever. My brother lives out in Colorado now, and he's always sending me pictures of his hikes. He bought these really expensive hiking boots last year, the kind with the special grip soles. They cost him like three hundred dollars, but he slipped on some ice anyway and sprained his ankle really bad. He had to wear this big plastic walking boot for six weeks. It looked exactly like a ski boot. I really don't understand how anyone is supposed to drive a car wearing one of those things. The pedals are so close together. 

Anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, I don't really get pleasure from those things anymore. Now I mostly just keep my face straight at work. I say only what I absolutely have to say to get the orders in and get back to the kitchen. And when my brother texts me those pictures, I just let the messages sit there. I see the notification, but I just don't feel the pull to answer him at all. I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Weight? Um... I guess my eating has been all over the place lately. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal. We usually get a free meal during our shift, which sounds like a great perk, right? But it's usually just whatever the kitchen needs to get rid of before it goes bad. Last week they made this massive batch of chicken piccata, but they put way too many capers in it. Capers are so weird, aren't they? They're like these little salty green peas that burst in your mouth. I read somewhere that they're actually pickled flower buds. I don't know who looked at a flower bud and thought, "Let's soak this in vinegar for a month and put it on chicken," but it's a very strange concept when you really think about it. Vinegar is another thing—my grandma used to swear by cleaning windows with vinegar and newspaper. She’d save up stacks of the Sunday paper just for that. The ink would get all over your hands and turn them gray. 

But anyway, yeah, some weeks I don't eat the staff meal at all. But then other nights, I'll come home after a long shift and I'll just eat whatever is in the kitchen just to feel settled. Like I'll just stand in front of the fridge and eat cold leftovers or half a box of stale cereal, just trying to feel... I don't know, grounded, I guess. So I don't really know if my weight has changed on the scale, but my eating is definitely just... all over the place.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

Moving slowly? Um... yeah, I guess so. Or sometimes the opposite. People at work have definitely noticed. Like, my manager, Brenda, she pulled me aside the other day. Brenda's been managing that place for like fifteen years, and she wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she points at something. She buys them at those little artisan craft fairs they have downtown on the weekends. I went to one of those fairs once, years ago, and bought this hand-carved wooden owl, but it smelled so strongly of varnish that I had to leave it out on the balcony for a month. The sun ended up bleaching half of its face white, so now it looks like some kind of phantom owl. 

But anyway, Brenda told me I've been acting weird on the floor. Like, sometimes I'll just pace around, checking the same tables and reorganizing the little sugar caddies and looking at the same receipts over and over. But then other times, I just get so... bogged down. Like, just grabbing menus from the host stand and walking over to the POS system feels like I'm moving through molasses, and it takes me way longer than it should. It's like my body just forgets how to move at a normal speed.
Do you find it harder to make decisions than you used to?

Decisions? Um... yeah, I guess. It’s more like my brain just kind of stalls out on me. Like, I’m having a lot of trouble just keeping numbers straight on the POS and the inventory sheets. 

The inventory sheets are always kept on these really cheap, flimsy clipboards. We have this one clipboard where the spring is totally shot, so the paper just slides right out if you hold it at the wrong angle. I don’t know why Brenda doesn’t just buy a new one. You can get them at the dollar store for literally a dollar. I went to the dollar store last week to get some dish soap, and they had this whole aisle of cheap plastic toys. It totally reminded me of those little prize bins at the dentist's office when you were a kid. I always used to pick those sticky hands that you throw against the wall, but they get covered in lint and dog hair after like five minutes, and then you just have to throw them away. They leave a weird greasy mark on the drywall, too. My mom used to get so mad about that... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the numbers. Yeah, I’ll just stand there and stare at the POS screen, knowing I’ve done this job for years, but I just can't trust what I just entered. Like, I can't decide if I did it right or not, and I just freeze up over something incredibly simple.
Have you had periods of feeling this low before, or is this the first time?

Feeling this low before? Um... well, it hasn't always been exactly like this, but yeah, this whole heavy, guilty, depressed feeling... it's been hanging around for about a year and two months now. A year and two months. That's right around the time my sister adopted that rescue dog, actually. A greyhound mix. They're so weird, greyhounds, aren't they? They're basically just skin and bones and they shiver all the time, even when it's warm out. She bought him this little knit sweater with a reindeer on it, which is cute in December, but she makes him wear it in July. I tried to tell her that dogs regulate their body temperature through panting and the pads of their feet, but she wouldn't listen. She never listens. When we were kids, she decided she wanted to build a treehouse, but instead of using nails, she tried to use Elmer's glue and duct tape. It held up for exactly one afternoon until it rained, and then the whole thing just slid down the trunk of the oak tree like a mudslide. We got in so much trouble because it crushed my dad's prize-winning tomato plants... 

But anyway, yeah, it's been about fourteen months of feeling this way. This low, guilty feeling. It just kind of settled in and never really left.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

Voices? Um... yeah, actually. Sometimes I do. It usually happens when I'm closing up the restaurant, or just sitting alone in my condo. I'll hear this low voice say my name, or whisper that I'm going to lose everything. It sounds so real that I actually turn around to check if someone's there. 

My condo is so quiet, too. I bought it back when interest rates were really low, which was lucky, I guess. The only problem is the HOA fees keep going up every year, and for what? They're supposed to maintain the landscaping, but the bushes out front have been dead since last summer. It's this weird type of holly bush, and the leaves get super brittle and sharp when they die. I scratched my leg on one just taking the trash out last week. I had to put a band-aid on it, but the only ones I had were those cheap plastic ones that don't breathe at all, so my skin got all white and pruney underneath. I usually buy the fabric ones, but I must have grabbed the wrong box at the pharmacy. The pharmacy is always so chaotic anyway, with the fluorescent lights buzzing and people coughing everywhere. I always feel like I'm going to catch something just standing in line. 

But yeah, the voice... it just whispers that I'm going to lose it all. And it sounds like it's right right behind me.
Do you ever see things that aren't really there when you're alone or hearing those voices?

See things? Um, no, I don't think I see anything. It's just the voices. Like I was saying, when I'm closing up the restaurant or just sitting alone in my condo, I'll hear that low voice say my name. Or it whispers that I'm going to lose everything. And it sounds so real that I turn around to check if someone is standing right there. 

There was this one time I turned around so fast I knocked over a whole tray of water glasses at the server station. They shattered everywhere. The glass we use at the restaurant is so thin, it practically explodes when it hits the tile. We get them from this supplier in Ohio, I think. Or maybe it's Iowa. Somewhere in the Midwest. The shipping costs must be astronomical, honestly. I don't know why the owner doesn't just go to a local restaurant supply store. There's one right off the highway next to that old abandoned mall. The mall has been empty for years, except for this one sad little pretzel stand that somehow manages to stay open. I bought a pretzel there once, and it was so stale I could barely bite into it. It was like chewing on a piece of rope. I remember trying to feed it to a seagull in the parking lot, but even the bird wouldn't eat it. Seagulls usually eat anything, you know? They're basically rats with wings. I saw one fly off with a whole slice of pizza once... 

But yeah, I don't see anything. I just hear the voice, and it sounds so real I have to look behind me.
Has this feeling of heaviness and worthlessness been constant over the past year and two months, or have you had periods where it lifted for a while?

Um... constant? Well, no, not exactly constant. There was this one stretch... maybe for several weeks? Yeah, a few weeks where I actually wasn't feeling so heavy and depressed. I was getting through my shifts at the restaurant a lot better, which was a relief because we were so short-staffed right around then. The manager, Gary, he kept scheduling me for these back-to-back double shifts. Gary is always messing up the schedule, though. He uses this ancient Excel spreadsheet from like, 2010, and he refuses to upgrade to the new scheduling app all the other restaurants use. I tried to show it to him on my phone once, but he just waved me off. He's one of those guys who still uses a flip phone. Can you believe that? He says he likes the physical buttons, but I'm pretty sure he just doesn't want to pay for a data plan. Data plans are such a rip-off anyway. My cell phone bill went up twenty bucks last month for absolutely no reason. 

But anyway, yeah, my mood was actually okay for those few weeks. I was getting through work fine. But the weird thing was... I was still hearing the whispering at the condo. That didn't stop at all. And I still had this awful feeling of being watched whenever I looked over my mortgage paperwork. The mortgage company keeps sending me these letters about my escrow account, and the envelopes have those little plastic windows on them. I really hate those envelopes. They never rip open cleanly, you know? You try to use your thumb and it just tears the paper in this jagged line, and then you have to fish the letter out. I bought a letter opener once, one of those heavy brass ones that looks like a little sword, but I lost it when I moved in. I think it fell behind the stove or something, but I'm not going to pull the whole stove out just to look for it. The gas line back there looks really old. 

But yeah, even when the depressed feeling lifted for a bit, the whispering and that feeling of being watched while I went through the mortgage papers... that was all still there.
Have you ever seen things that other people can't see when you're hearing those voices?

See things? Um, no, I don't think so. I'm pretty sure you asked me that already, but no, I don't see anything. It's just the voices. Like I said, it's usually when I'm closing up the restaurant or just sitting alone in my condo. I'll hear that low voice say my name, or whisper that I'm going to lose everything. And it sounds so real that I turn around to check if someone is standing right there. 

It's actually kind of annoying because it always makes me jump. I spilled a whole cup of coffee on my favorite rug last week because I thought someone was right behind me. It's this really nice Persian rug I found at an estate sale. The lady running the sale was so rude, though. She kept following me around the house like I was going to steal something. I mean, who steals a rug? It's huge. You can't just stuff it in your pocket. I had to rent a van just to get it home. The rental place smelled like stale cigarette smoke and cheap pine air freshener. It gave me a massive headache. I tried rolling the windows down, but the crank on the passenger side was broken. It just spun around and around without doing anything. It's crazy how they rent out vehicles in that condition. I should have complained, but I was just so tired from working all weekend. 

But yeah, no, I don't see anything. Just the voice whispering to me.
Have you had other periods like this in your life before the past year and two months?

Um, before this? No, not really. This whole thing... like, these depressed, guilty periods where I just feel awful? It's really just been this one stretch for about a year and two months now. 

I remember because it started right around the time I had to get my emissions tested on my Civic. The DMV sent me that renewal postcard, and I always forget to update my address with them, so it went to my old apartment first. My old landlord actually had to forward it to me. He's this really grumpy guy named Stan who breeds pugs. Have you ever been around a bunch of pugs? They make this awful snorting sound when they breathe, like they're constantly choking. Stan had like five of them just waddling around his living room, shedding this coarse beige hair all over the furniture. I sat on his couch once to sign my lease, and when I stood up, my black work slacks looked like I was wearing fur pants. I had to use a whole roll of lint roller tape before my shift at the restaurant. Lint rollers are getting so expensive now, too. The brand-name ones are like six dollars, and the cheap ones don't even stick to anything. You roll it over your pants and it just pushes the hair around instead of picking it up... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, before a year and two months ago, I never really felt this heavy and guilty. It's just been this one time.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see at the same time?

Well, yeah, like I was saying before, the voices are definitely there. And the thing is, during those really awful, heavy stretches where I'm just so depressed I can barely move, the whispering is still happening at the same time. I'll be sitting there feeling totally worthless, and the voice is right there telling me I'm going to lose the condo, or I'll get that intense feeling that the mortgage company or Gary is watching me. So I'm basically dealing with both things at once while I'm just trying to drag myself through my shifts at the restaurant. 

It's exhausting, honestly. Working in food service is draining enough without all that. You're on your feet for eight hours straight, carrying these massive trays. We have these oval trays for big parties, and they are so unbalanced. If someone puts a heavy plate of ribs on one side and just a side salad on the other, the whole thing tilts. I dropped a whole tray of waters once because of that. Ice went everywhere. It was right in front of this table of teenagers who were already being super obnoxious, leaving straw wrappers all over the floor. I don't understand why kids do that. They just tear the top off the straw and blow the paper at each other. It gets stuck to the wet floor and then you have to scrape it up with a mop. Our mop bucket at work is broken, too. The wringer part squeaks so loud it sounds like a dying bird, and one of the wheels is stuck, so you just end up dragging it across the tile and leaving these long black scuff marks. Gary said he'd order a new one three months ago, but of course he hasn't. 

But yeah, to answer your question, when the depression is at its absolute worst, the whispering and the feeling of being watched don't stop. They're all happening together.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this depressed and guilty, or is this the only time?

Well, like I was saying before, it's really just been this one long stretch. But, um, yeah, for most of this whole period... even when I have a day or two that feels a little lighter, I've been weighed down by that empty, guilty feeling more often than not. It just hangs over me. 

Kind of like the weather we've been having lately, actually. It's just been so gray and overcast for weeks. I tried to buy one of those sun lamps online, the ones that are supposed to help your mood? But the shipping got delayed twice. The first time, the tracking said it was "out for delivery," and I waited around the condo all day on my day off. I didn't even go down to the lobby to get my mail because I was afraid I'd miss the delivery guy. Our buzzer system is broken, so they usually just leave a sticky note on the glass door. The property management company is supposed to fix it, but they're useless. They raised our HOA fees by fifty dollars last month and for what? The landscaping is a mess. The bushes out front are totally overgrown and scratching up against the brick. Someone threw a fast-food cup in there last week and it's just sitting there because the landscaping crew just uses leaf blowers instead of actually picking up trash. Those leaf blowers are so loud, too. They start at like 7 AM on Tuesdays. 

But yeah, anyway, the depression thing... it's just been this one long period where that heavy, guilty feeling is there most of the time.

patient.answer:
Um, yeah, hi. I guess... I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage recently, and... well, the yard is actually a lot bigger than we thought. There's this huge oak tree in the back, and our neighbor keeps complaining about the leaves blowing onto his driveway. He drives this pristine vintage Corvette, which, honestly, why park it outside if you're so worried about leaves, right? He's out there with a leaf blower every single morning at 7 AM. 

But anyway, yeah, I just feel like every small mistake I make at work proves I’m completely useless and just... deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me. I'm waiting tables right now, and the other day I accidentally dropped a tray of water glasses. The ice went everywhere, under the booths... and they have that really cheap carpeting in the dining room that takes forever to dry. It smells like old soup when it gets wet. I don't know why the owner doesn't just put in hardwood or tile, it would be so much easier to sweep up at closing time. We're always there an extra hour just vacuuming. So, yeah... I don't know.

doctor.intent: determine the duration of the patient's current feelings of uselessness
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling like you're useless and deserving of bad things?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, guilty periods have been present for about 1 year and 2 months of this whole time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the depressive symptoms (feeling useless and deserving of bad things).

patient.answer:
Well, the really depressed, guilty feelings... I'd say it's been about a year and two months of feeling like this. Which, actually, is exactly when they hired the new manager at the restaurant. Gary. He's the one who decided we all needed to wear these awful polyester uniforms instead of just our own black shirts. Polyester doesn't breathe at all, you know? Especially when you're carrying hot plates back and forth from the kitchen all night. 

The kitchen is always like eighty-five degrees anyway because the ventilation hood above the fryers has been making this horrible rattling noise and barely working since Thanksgiving. The repair guy came out once, looked at it with a flashlight for maybe five minutes, and said he needed to order a special part from Germany or something. That was months ago. I bet he never even ordered it, he just wanted the call-out fee. But yeah... it's been about a year and two months of just feeling completely worthless like that.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like I’m going through the motions carrying plates and smiling because I’m supposed to, not because I feel anything good.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of pleasure or interest), which is a core feature of a depressive episode and aligns with the patient's persistent empty mood and inability to feel anything good.

patient.answer:
Um, pleasure? No, not really. I mean, most days there's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Just carrying plates, smiling at customers because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. Which is hard, because you have to smile for tips.

doctor.question: Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this depressed and guilty, or is this the only time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: For most of this whole period, even when some days were lighter, I’ve been weighed down by that empty, guilty feeling more often than not.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there have been multiple periods of depression or just one continuous period, which relates to determining if the depressive episode has been present for the majority of the total duration of the illness.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was saying before, it's really just been this one long stretch. But, um, yeah, for most of this whole period... even when I have a day or two that feels a little lighter, I've been weighed down by that empty, guilty feeling more often than not. It just hangs over me. 

Kind of like the weather we've been having lately, actually. It's just been so gray and overcast for weeks. I tried to buy one of those sun lamps online, the ones that are supposed to help your mood? But the shipping got delayed twice. The first time, the tracking said it was "out for delivery," and I waited around the condo all day on my day off. I didn't even go down to the lobby to get my mail because I was afraid I'd miss the delivery guy. Our buzzer system is broken, so they usually just leave a sticky note on the glass door. The property management company is supposed to fix it, but they're useless. They raised our HOA fees by fifty dollars last month and for what? The landscaping is a mess. The bushes out front are totally overgrown and scratching up against the brick. Someone threw a fast-food cup in there last week and it's just sitting there because the landscaping crew just uses leaf blowers instead of actually picking up trash. Those leaf blowers are so loud, too. They start at like 7 AM on Tuesdays. 

But yeah, anyway, the depression thing... it's just been this one long period where that heavy, guilty feeling is there most of the time.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and depression, which have been present for over a year. The patient also reports a lack of pleasure in activities, significant weight changes, and fatigue, which are all characteristic of a major depressive episode.
